messages:
Diego: Hi team 1st day question. My new USB-C -> GigE dongle from the kit isn't showing up in Network prefs on my MacBook (Monterey). USB Accessories shows the device when I plug it in but no interface in System Settings. Any quick fixes?

it-ops: Welcome Diego! Quick checks: 1) which dongle model (label on box)? 2) can you run `system_profiler SPUSBDataType` and paste the block for the adapter?

Diego: Model is UniLink-GT100. system_profiler shows it under USB Device Tree as "Ethernet Adapter (Vendor: UniLink)" with idVendor/idProduct 0x1a2b/0x3c4d. No interface in Network.

it-ops: Ok that means the OS sees the USB device but the kernel driver may not have bound. On Monterey try: 1) open Terminal and run `sudo ifconfig -a` and see if a new `enX` shows; 2) If not, try resetting the USB stack: `sudo kextunload -b com.apple.driver.AppleUSBHostMergeProperties || true; sudo kextload -b com.apple.driver.AppleUSBHostMergeProperties` then replug.

Diego: Ran `ifconfig -a` 
didn't show anything new. Tried the kextunload/load sequence, then unplug/replug. Still nothing.

it-bot: New IT ticket #44902 created: "UniLink-GT100 not exposing network interface on MacBook" assigned to it-ops.

it-ops: Thanks. Two fast workarounds: 1) If you have Wi-Fi hotspot on your phone, enable it and join to finish onboarding. 2) I can request a tested spare USB-Ethernet (different chipset) and a USB-A adapter if needed. Are you in SF or remote?

Diego: I'm remote in Portland. Hotspot workaround works for now. Could you ship the spare adapter? Also who do I ping for static DHCP reservation for my home VPN lease?

it-ops: I'll set up the spare test unit and ship priority USPS with tracking. ETA 3 business days. For DHCP reservation/VPN lease ping infra-network or DM me and I'll open the internal request. Note: if you often need wired for latency-sensitive work, the spare will be a different chipset (Realtek vs ASIX) which usually resolves driver issues.

laura-facilities: tagging for equipment pickup/shipment: we'll include a prepaid return label for the faulty dongle in the box. Please keep the original accessory bag if possible.

Diego: Thanks all. One more thing 50% of my home Wi-Fi packets seem to drop when uploading large corp packages (S3). Any recommended laptop settings while testing wired vs wireless?

it-ops: For testing: 1) run `iperf3` to the Redwood test endpoint (I'll DM details). 2) For Wi-Fi, try disabling 802.11n/ax in router if possible to force stable rates; for mac, `sudo sysctl -w net.inet.tcp.delayed_ack=0` can help with uploads for old APs (revert after test). Keep us logs and we'll compare once the spare arrives.

Diego: Great, I'll run iperf3 and share results. Appreciate the quick turnaround on the spare and the label. :+1:
